_readme: The machine-readable inventory of the autonomous suite. CHARTER.md is the contract;
this file is the part of it a script can check, and scripts/routine-registry-guard.cjs
(pnpm guard:routines, in the required CI gate) is what checks it.
Why it exists: CHARTER §0's failure was a suite that stopped and described itself as live
for five weeks. §7 answers 'did it run' from reports. Nothing answered the question one
step earlier — 'does this routine still have a definition anyone but one laptop can read?'
On 2026-08-18, six of the ten scheduled routines existed only under ~/.claude/
scheduled-tasks/ on the founder's machine: unversioned, unreviewable, and unrunnable from
any cloud session. Each of those carries a dated waiver below rather than a silence.
WHAT THIS FILE IS NOT. It is not the fleet-2 schedule. Claude-Code-Remote triggers are
authoritative in list_triggers (CHARTER §3) and a hand-copied cron here would rot within
a day. Fleet-2 rows record only the CONTRACT — which repo-native skill the trigger must
invoke — because that is the half the repo can actually verify.
Adding/retiring/re-timing a routine edits this file, CHARTER §3, and the scheduler

waiver.reason: Definition lives only in ~/.claude/scheduled-tasks/launch-gate/ on the founder's machine. It publishes §7's RELEASABLE line — the suite's headline output — from a file no reviewer, no guard and no cloud session can read.
waiver.remedy: Commit it to .claude/skills/launch-gate/SKILL.md and point the scheduled task at the repo copy, as primary-engineer and compliance-watch already are.

routines.title: Frontend Wiring Audit
routines.note: taskId is deliberately unwieldy and deliberately unrenamed (CHARTER §3) — renaming discards its run history and stored tool approvals. The id here is its taskId prefix.

waiver.reason: Writes code on the capture path daily — the highest-consequence lane in the suite after Primary Engineer — from an unversioned definition. Its rails cannot be reviewed in a PR or checked by any guard.
waiver.remedy: Commit to .claude/skills/frontend-wiring-audit/SKILL.md; keep the scheduler taskId unchanged so run history and approvals survive.

waiver.reason: Owns acceptance question A (does an organic file reach a lender clean) and may ship small/safe fixes. Unversioned.

Feeds every verified row in feature-review/FINDINGS.md, which Primary Engineer builds from. Its adversarial-verification method is unversioned, so a drift in it silently changes what the whole suite treats as a verified finding.
waiver.remedy: Commit to .claude/skills/deliverable-qa-sweep/SKILL.md; the .claude/agents/{feature-reviewer,finding-verifier,workflow-verifier}.md it drives are already in the repo, which makes the missing half conspicuous.

waiver.reason: Holds exclusive authority over CTO_ROADMAP.md §0–§3 and performs §7's proof-of-life count — the control that would have caught §0's five-week silence — from an unversioned file.
waiver.remedy: Commit to .claude/skills/evening-triage/SKILL.md. Highest-value of the six: it is the only routine whose absence hides the absence of the others.

waiver.reason: Report-only, so the blast radius is lowest of the six — but it is still a routine whose rails nobody can read.

routines.title: Sprint Blitz
routines.note: Absorbed into Primary Engineer (CHARTER §3, §11 worked example). Registered here only so its historical reports are not read as orphans.

routines.title: Financial Audit
routines.cadence: monthly (1st) — schedule authoritative in list_triggers, never here
routines.note: Governed by CHARTER §6's Financial Audit row. Rewired 2026-08-18 to invoke the repo skill instead of carrying a private copy of the method.

routines.title: Doc Accuracy steward
routines.cadence: 6-hourly, plus a Monday firing — schedule authoritative in list_triggers, never here

awaiting.note: Two triggers invoke this skill (the 6-hourly steward and the Monday 14:00 firing) and it does not exist on origin/main. Both are correctly written to say so and stop, which is the right shape — but that is ~29 no-op runs a week until the founding PR merges, and a second Monday firing 100 minutes before a steward tick is duplication to resolve when it does.

routines.title: Better.com competitive brief
routines.cadence: daily — schedule authoritative in list_triggers, never here
routines.note: Report-only; may file one design-standard issue. Still carries its method in the trigger prompt rather than a repo skill — a drift risk the audit records but does not fix.

routines.title: Page-by-page deep inspection
routines.cadence: daily — schedule authoritative in list_triggers, never here
routines.note: Files page-audit issues; opens no PRs. Its 10-slot rotation and defect-class list live in the trigger prompt — the largest private method copy in either fleet.

routines.title: UX audit vs the design standard
routines.cadence: weekly (Wed) — schedule authoritative in list_triggers, never here
routines.note: Report-only, read access. Duplicates DESIGN_SYSTEM.md §13's four questions in prose; the standard itself wins on any conflict.

routines.title: Logged-in Better deep-dive reminder
routines.cadence: weekly (Mon) — schedule authoritative in list_triggers, never here
routines.note: Human-directed; sends a reminder and nothing else. Never handles a sign-in.

routines.title: PR sync & review loop
routines.cadence: hourly on weekdays — schedule authoritative in list_triggers, never here
routines.note: Updates open PR branches and reports a digest. Never merges. This is the fleet-2 routine that most needs CHARTER §5's assist ladder in a repo skill.
